title: Dan Bilzerian
subtitle: Public profile, the 2026 Florida primary, and a reported insignia
summary: A sourced public-record profile of Dan Bilzerian, a social media personality who ran as a Republican against Representative Randy Fine in the 18 August 2026 primary for Florida’s 6th Congressional District. Official results, follower counts and reporting are cited with dates and links. A reported Nazi insignia is presented as attributed reporting, not as a finding of this page. Questions are asked; they are not conclusions.
scope: A public-record profile, not a verdict and not a court. A journalist’s description, a campaign remark and an author’s view are different things. Inclusion is not a judgment of character. This page does not find that Bilzerian is, or is not, a Nazi.
status_note: Sources reviewed on 14 November 2026. The X follower count is taken from X’s public profile metrics on that date. This page does not adopt commentators’ labels as statements of fact, and it does not treat a reported insignia as proof of a political identity. It is not legal advice.

sections.title: Who he is
sections.intro: A short public-record sketch of Dan Bilzerian’s identity and public profile, confined to sourced biographical facts and current follower counts. It is not a judgment of character.

paragraphs.text: Daniel Brandon Bilzerian was born on 7 December 1980 in Tampa, Florida. He is an American social media personality and poker player. In the 2010s he became widely known for documenting an extravagant lifestyle on Instagram; on 10 December 2014 CNBC referred to him as the “King of Instagram,” a nickname that later also appears on his campaign biography. This page uses that phrase only as a published description, not as a finding of its own.

sections.title: The 2026 Republican primary
sections.intro: Bilzerian ran as a Republican, not as an independent, against incumbent Representative Randy Fine in Florida’s 6th Congressional District. The figures below are the official, certified results.

paragraphs.text: The Federal Election Commission’s candidate record lists Daniel Brandon Bilzerian as a Republican challenger for Florida’s 6th Congressional District in the 2026 cycle, candidate ID H6FL06415, with a first filing date of 7 April 2026 and party “REPUBLICAN PARTY.” Ballotpedia records that he lost the Republican primary on 18 August 2026.

sources.locator: H6FL06415, party REP, office House, district 06, first_file_date 2026-04-07, incumbent_challenge Challenger
Daniel Bilzerian (Republican Party) ran for Florida’s 6th District and lost in the Republican primary on 18 August 2026

paragraphs.text: The Florida Division of Elections published official results for the 18 August 2026 Republican primary in Florida’s 6th Congressional District. Randy Fine won and advanced as the Republican nominee, with 51,109 votes (57.6%). Dan Bilzerian, listed as a Republican candidate and not as an independent, finished second, with 16,776 votes (18.9%). Aaron Baker received 12,074 votes (13.6%) and Charles Gambaro 8,716 votes (9.8%). The four-candidate total is 88,675 votes. A dedicated public-record profile of Randy Fine is on this site’s Randy Fine page.

sections.title: A reported Nazi insignia
sections.intro: This section records what was publicly reported, by whom and when, about Nazi insignia said to have appeared on a paintball marker in Bilzerian’s collection. The descriptions are those of the cited reporters and of a person who posted the video. They are not findings of this page. This page does not reproduce images of the markings.

entries.title: May 2025 · reporting of a paintball marker

paragraphs.text: On 12 May 2025, The Paintball Post reported that an Instagram story published earlier that week by Marcello Margott, described as a host of the Play the Game podcast, featured a tour of Bilzerian’s paintball gear collection, and that viewers had noticed “one particular marker in the mix. A Planet Eclipse CS3 with Nazi iconography, right down to a swastika on the feedneck.” The article’s editor’s note said a photograph accompanying that article was “not from Margott’s post, but it is a picture of the marker in question.” This page repeats those words as The Paintball Post’s, not as a finding of its own.

sources.locator: “Does Paintball Have A Nazi Problem?”, 12 May 2025, “The smoking gun”

paragraphs.text: On 14 May 2025, Hannah Feuer reported in the Forward that the controversy started when Margott, described there as a paintball world champion and as Bilzerian’s trainee, “posted an Instagram story last week displaying his trainee Dan Bilzerian’s vast collection of paintball equipment,” and that viewers “noticed a paintball gun decorated with Nazi insignia — including the Nazi Eagle, SS Bolts, and Celtic Cross.” The Forward reported that, on the Tuesday of that week, the National Paintball League (NXL) created a new rule prohibiting “displaying offensive, inappropriate, or discriminatory content during any NXL-sanctioned event,” and that Margott was removed from the roster of the professional team Edmonton Impact.

sources.locator: Hannah Feuer, 14 May 2025, description of Margott’s Instagram story and the NXL rule

paragraphs.text: The Forward quoted an Instagram statement from Margott in which he wrote that he did not notice the paintball gun in his video until it was pointed out to him the next day: “I do not condone any symbol of hate, period.” The Forward also reported that he added that he believes “in having friends with different world views,” and that he “did not commit to stop coaching Bilzerian.” Those are Margott’s words and the Forward’s characterisation, not findings of this page.

sources.locator: Margott’s Instagram statement as quoted by Hannah Feuer, 14 May 2025

paragraphs.text: The Paintball Post noted that “many have started hunting for the company that did the anodizing job on the marker,” and warned that “false accusations can live on long after they are disproven.” This page does not determine who applied the markings, when they were applied, or why. Provenance — including whether the work was commissioned, how it entered the collection, or what happened along a supply chain — is not established here.

sources.locator: 12 May 2025, “What to do about witch hunts”

paragraphs.text: This page checked Bilzerian’s X account, @DanBilzerian, for posts in May 2025 using terms including paintball, marker, Margott, swastika and insignia, and did not locate a public post in that window explaining, confirming or denying the markings. It has not located a later public denial or explanation from him that addresses this specific report. The absence of a located statement is not itself a finding about what he believes. Later commentators applied labels to Bilzerian in other contexts, including campaign reporting; those labels are not adopted here, and they are not treated as a second documented insignia display. The sources located for this section describe one reported instance, in May 2025. That is a statement about the sources located, not a finding that no other instance exists.

entries.title: Can someone display a Nazi insignia without being a Nazi?

paragraphs.text: The question this section will not pretend to answer as a finding is: can someone display a Nazi insignia without being a Nazi? Context and provenance matter to that question — a single object in a collection, marks whose author is not established here, and the difference between one reported instance and a pattern — but they do not dispose of it. Displaying such insignia is not treated lightly on this page, and nothing that follows is a justification or an endorsement of Nazi symbols, Nazi politics, or hatred of Jewish people.

The author’s view, which is not a conclusion of this page, is set out in the disclosure below: for him, one isolated instance is not decisive. That is his opinion. It is not a finding that the report was false, that the markings were accidental, or that further instances would be irrelevant. The question remains open.

sections.title: Author’s disclosure
sections.intro: This is a first-person statement by Mars Robertson, the author of IndependentTribunal.org, about his position in the 2026 Republican primary. It is his own account, clearly marked as such, and not a finding of this page.

entries.title: A statement in the author’s own name

paragraphs.text: My support was strategic and conditional. Even after I was made aware of the Nazi insignia, I continued to support Bilzerian, consistent with my strategy. For me, one isolated instance is not decisive. I do not support Nazis. If more Nazi material appears I will re-evaluate. Official election records, set out above, show that Bilzerian ran as a Republican in the 18 August 2026 primary, not as an independent candidate. This is my own statement, not a finding of this page about any person.

The YouTube listing for this video, on the channel Mars Robertson (genesis.re) at @genesisdotre, is titled “Why do I support Bilzerian?” YouTube’s video page lists the upload date as 28 May 2026, 17:50 Pacific Daylight Time (29 May 2026, 00:50 UTC) and the duration as 4 minutes 39 seconds. The published description reads: “Follow me on Twitter: https://x.com/MarsitaTheUltra/status/2060160929245909437” and “Clips from: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=llYEEX2lws8”. This page records that listing. It does not treat the video or those clips as a transcript, and it does not describe footage that has not been independently verified here.
